name: When should I replace interior trim instead of just repainting it?

mainEntity.name: When should I replace interior trim instead of just repainting it?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing your interior trim if it shows signs of physical damage, water swelling, or outdated sizing that clashes with a remodel. Dents from vacuums, pet scratches, and warped MDF from bathroom moisture cannot always be repaired with wood filler. Additionally, many older homes have narrow 2.5-inch baseboards that look out of proportion under modern 8- or 9-foot ceilings. Upgrading to taller, squared, or multi-piece baseboards instantly refreshes the room and cleanly transitions into updated doors, cabinets, and tile work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace trim when it has permanent water damage, deep gouges, or warping, or when upgrading to taller, modern profiles to match a broader home renovation.
